result.topic_en: Gauss gives an improved parametrization of a rotation matrix by four quantities a, b, c, d (half-sum square roots of the diagonal entries), states the composition rule for two such transformations (quaternion multiplication), and expresses a, b, c, d via the axis coordinates, magnification and rotation angle.
result.transcription:
Besser auf folgende Weise
[Vergl. oben Seite 114 Schering]
$\sqrt{\frac{1+p+q+r}{2}} = a$
$\sqrt{\frac{1+p-q-r}{2}} = b$
$\sqrt{\frac{1-p+q-r}{2}} = c$
$\sqrt{\frac{1-p-q+r}{2}} = d$

$\frac{1}{2}(aa+bb-cc-dd)$ | $-ad-bc$ | $-ac+bd$
$+ad-bc$ | $\frac{1}{2}(aa-bb+cc-dd)$ | $-ab-cd$
$+ac+bd$ | $+ab-cd$ | $\frac{1}{2}(aa-bb-cc+dd)$

Aus der Verbindung zweier Transformationen
deren erster die Scale $a, b, c, d$
— zweiter — $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ } entspricht
entsteht eine neue deren Scale
$a\alpha - b\beta - c\gamma - d\delta$
$a\beta + b\alpha - c\delta + d\gamma$
$a\gamma + b\delta + c\alpha - d\beta$
$a\delta - b\gamma + c\beta + d\alpha$

Sind die Coordinaten des ruhenden Punkts $\xi, \eta, \zeta$, Vergrösserung
$= nn$, Drehung $= \lambda$ so kann man setzen
$a = n \cos\frac{1}{2}\lambda$ [-$= \sqrt{(1+\cos\lambda)}$-]
$b = n\xi \sin\frac{1}{2}\lambda$ [-$\sqrt{(\xi\xi - \cos\lambda)}$-]
$c = n\eta \sin\frac{1}{2}\lambda$ [-$\sqrt{(\eta\eta - \cos\lambda)}$-]
$d = n\zeta \sin\frac{1}{2}\lambda$ [-$\sqrt{(\zeta\zeta - \cos\lambda)}$-]

(margin) Coordinat[?]

methods.what: Parametrization of rotation parameters a,b,c,d from diagonal entries p,q,r of the rotation matrix
Rotation (similarity) matrix expressed in four parameters a,b,c,d (Euler–Rodrigues form, with factor 1/2)
Composition of two transformations corresponds to quaternion-type multiplication of their 'scales'
methods.quote:
$a\alpha - b\beta - c\gamma - d\delta$
$a\beta + b\alpha - c\delta + d\gamma$
$a\gamma + b\delta + c\alpha - d\beta$
$a\delta - b\gamma + c\beta + d\alpha$

methods.what: Parameters in terms of fixed axis (ξ,η,ζ), magnification nn and rotation angle λ (half-angle formulas)

items.english: From the combination of two transformations, the first of which corresponds to the scale a, b, c, d and the second to α, β, γ, δ, there arises a new one whose scale is [the four expressions].
